plan.title: pre-pr:run ignores --project-root and always uses the cwd store

narratives.Description: pre-pr:run ignores --project-root and always uses the cwd store
narratives.Overview:
1. Default store by root (P1). `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot)` resolves `projectRoot` to an absolute path at call time, keeps that path with its one cached store, and builds the store from it. A call whose resolved root differs replaces the cached store with one for the new root. A store injected with `setDefaultPrePrStore` or `resetDefaultPrePrStore` is returned for any root until cleared. A new export `clearDefaultPrePrStore()` drops the cached and the injected store.
2. One root in `run()` (P1). `run()` resolves `projectRoot = args.projectRoot?.trim() || process.cwd()` once, before the first store use, and calls `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot)`. Push-admit, the observe gate checks, evaluate, complete and the story-line writer use that same value. `--body-file` paths stay relative to the cwd.
3. Semantic hash root (P1). `--observe-semantic` calls `computeControllerObservedHash({ reviewedFiles, cwd: projectRoot })`, so relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the root, as `completeRun` already re-hashes them.
4. Help text (P3). The `--project-root` usage line says it sets the root for the private store, the gate checks, relative `--reviewed-file` paths, `--complete` and `--push-admit`; that it defaults to the cwd; and that `--body-file` paths stay relative to the cwd.
5. Tests (P1, P2). With the default store cleared: start a run with cwd A; from cwd B with `--project-root A`, record a command phase and a semantic phase whose relative `--reviewed-file` also exists in B with different contents; both succeed, the rows are in A's store, and the hash is of A's file. From cwd B without `--project-root`, the run is reported missing. In one process, `getDefaultPrePrStore` called with A, then B, then A returns the store for each root, and a relative root resolves against the cwd at call time. The existing injected-store tests pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `--project-root <dir>`, `pre-pr:run` start, observe (command and semantic), evaluate and complete read and write the private store under `<dir>` from any cwd.
- Without `--project-root`, the store and relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the cwd as today.
- On `--observe-semantic`, relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the project root.
- `getDefaultPrePrStore` returns a store for the absolute root it is given unless a test store is injected, and `clearDefaultPrePrStore` removes both the cached and the injected store.
- A test starts a run in one directory and records a command phase and a semantic phase from another directory with `--project-root`, and both succeed.
- The `--project-root` help line names each use above and says `--body-file` paths stay relative to the cwd.
narratives.Constraint:
- Comparing or storing the raw `--project-root` string as the store identity (comment 7052371293, finding 1).
- Making `--body-file` project-relative (comment 7052371293, finding 2: it changes existing behaviour beyond this fix).

## In plain English
`deft pre-pr:run --help` says `--project-root` sets the project root for store resolution. It does not. Every path except `--push-admit` opens the private store from the current directory, so a call from any other directory fails with "pre-PR run <id> is not in the private store". Agent hosts that reset the cwd on every shell call must write `cd <worktree> && deft pre-pr:run …`, which a permission rule keyed on `deft pre-pr:run` does not cover.

The recommended fix: resolve the project root once (`--project-root`, else the cwd) and open the store from it on every path. Relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the same root, as `--complete` already does when it re-hashes them. The help text says so.

## Pains
- P1 — When `--project-root` is given, every `pre-pr:run` path (start, observe, complete, evaluate) resolves the private store from it.
- P2 — A test starts a run in one directory and records a phase from another directory with `--project-root`, and it succeeds.
- P3 — The help text matches the behaviour.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- Semantic-phase hashes, phase order, `merge_chokepoint`, finishing without a PR, and push-gate wording: #6893.
- What `--complete` does with `verify:ac`: #6888, in review as PR #6913.

## Constraints (not pains)
- No new flag, gate or policy. Without `--project-root`, behaviour does not change (the cwd stays the default).
- Coordinate with PR #6913: it edits the `--complete` block and the usage text of `pre-pr-run.ts`. This fix builds on top of it and leaves its `completeRun` changes alone.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts` 472: `const store = getDefaultPrePrStore();` with no argument, used by mark-complete, observe, evaluate, complete and start.
- `pre-pr-run.ts` 450, 507, 627, 645: `args.projectRoot?.trim() || process.cwd()` reaches only push-admit, the observe gate checks, `completeRun` and the story-line writer.
- `pre-pr-run.ts` 538: `computeControllerObservedHash({ reviewedFiles })` with no `cwd`, so relative reviewed files resolve against the cwd. `controller.ts` 1013-1021: `completeRun` re-hashes the same manifest with `cwd: options.projectRoot`.
- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/store.ts` 289-296: `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot = process.cwd())` caches one store per process and ignores the argument once a store exists; `setDefaultPrePrStore` / `resetDefaultPrePrStore` inject a test store.
- `packages/core/src/preflight-gh/pre-push.ts` 364: the push gate already calls `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot)`.
- `packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.test.ts` 92-102 inject a store per test; 427-452 pass `--project-root` to another directory and expect the row in the injected store.
- `pre-pr-run.ts` 73: usage line `--project-root <path>   project root for --push-admit / store resolution`.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1). `run()` resolves `projectRoot = args.projectRoot?.trim() || process.cwd()` once, before the first store use, and calls `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot)`. Every later branch uses that one value.
- R2 (P1). `getDefaultPrePrStore(projectRoot)` remembers the root of the store it created. A call with a different resolved root opens a store for that root instead of returning the cached one. A store injected with `setDefaultPrePrStore` or `resetDefaultPrePrStore` is still returned for any root, so hermetic tests keep working.
- R3 (P1). `--observe-semantic` hashes relative `--reviewed-file` paths against `projectRoot` (`computeControllerObservedHash({ reviewedFiles, cwd: projectRoot })`), the same root `completeRun` re-hashes them against.
- R4 (P3). The usage line says `--project-root` sets the root for the private store, the gate checks, relative `--reviewed-file` paths, `--complete` and `--push-admit`, and defaults to the cwd.
- R5 (P2). Tests with no injected store: start a run with the cwd in directory A; from cwd B, record a command phase and a semantic phase with relative `--reviewed-file` and `--project-root A`; both succeed and the rows are in A's store. A call from cwd B without `--project-root` still reports the run missing.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is R2 needed, or is one store per CLI process enough? Is there a lighter test seam than a root-keyed cache (for example a clear function, or a store factory on `PrePrRunOptions`)?
2. R3 changes where relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve when the cwd differs from the root. Is that safe for callers who run from a subdirectory today, given that `completeRun` already hashes against the root?
3. Does anything else in the four paths still read the cwd (for example `--evaluate`, the story-line writer's `--body-file`, or `git` calls in the controller)?

## In plain English

`--project-root` currently selects some checks but not the private store. A command launched elsewhere therefore cannot find the intended run. The proposed shared root and matching semantic-file hashing address that defect. I support the mechanism with two framing clarifications; I found no design blocker.

Answers to Stop 1:

1. R2 is unnecessary for a fresh process executing one CLI command, but appropriate for repeated in-process calls and the shared store API. A single cached store plus its absolute root and an explicit injection override is sufficient; a multi-root cache is unnecessary. A clear function helps tests but does not itself fix production root switching.
2. R3 is appropriate because completion already interprets relative reviewed files against the selected root. Explicit-root callers using subdirectory-relative paths will need root-relative or absolute paths. Calls without the flag retain their existing interpretation.
3. `--body-file` remains cwd-relative in both start and evaluate. The inspected controller deletion-diff Git call already receives the project root. PR #6913’s supplied diff can retain its controller-owned `verify:ac` behavior while consuming the shared root.

All code references below are at `880c91ed079578e900c1f2ef680efbfa6e6d61af`. Verification used pinned reads only; no tests, writes, or network access.

### 1. sharpens-framing — Root identity must remain stable across cwd changes

Evidence: `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/store.ts:171–175` retains the supplied root string; lines 205 and 242 resolve it during later operations. Lines 289–305 implement the singleton and injection seams. The push gate also consumes this singleton at `packages/core/src/preflight-gh/pre-push.ts:364–366`.

Concrete failure mode: comparing a cached raw `"."` against a later `"."` after changing cwd can reuse the wrong store identity. Comparing absolute roots while constructing the store with the original relative string can instead make a retained store drift when cwd changes. This matters to worktree isolation, not merely test convenience.

Disposition: R2 can bind with “resolved root” explicitly meaning an absolute path captured at selection time and used for both comparison and store construction. One replaceable cache entry suffices. Injected stores remain explicit overrides. Coverage should include switching A→B→A in one process and a relative-root case.

The strongest argument for omitting R2 is the one-command-per-process CLI lifecycle. That would be sufficient if the shared API were restricted to that lifecycle; the exported `run()` and shared accessor do not establish that restriction.

### 2. sharpens-framing — The fix does not make every file argument project-relative

Evidence: `packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts:575–577` and `660–663` read `args.bodyFile` directly. `packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:1228–1229` reads that same argument, and lines 1293–1296 resolve its write destination against cwd.

Concrete failure mode: from directory B, `--project-root A --body-file body.md` still reads or modifies B’s file, or fails if it is absent. Store selection can be correct while this command still surprises a caller expecting complete cwd independence.

Disposition: the design can bind with this boundary explicit. Keeping body-file paths cwd-relative preserves existing behavior and avoids expanding this fix; absolute body-file paths support cross-directory calls. R4 should distinguish project-relative reviewed files from cwd-relative body-file arguments.

### 3. footnote — R3 fixes an existing observation/completion mismatch

`packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts:538` hashes against cwd, while `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.ts:1013–1018` re-hashes against the explicit root. Lines 198–205 preserve absolute paths and include the supplied manifest spelling in the digest.

R3 aligns these operations. A useful regression fixture gives A and B different contents at the same relative filename, proving that observation selects A rather than merely finding a readable file.

### 4. footnote — R5 needs genuinely uninjected execution

`packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.test.ts:92–102` injects a store before each test, and `resetDefaultPrePrStore()` installs an in-memory store rather than clearing the override (`store.ts:302–305`).

Consequently, the current suite setup cannot demonstrate production root selection unchanged. Fresh-process tests or an explicit override-clearing seam can provide that coverage. Preserving injection behavior remains compatible with the existing test at lines 427–448.

### 5. footnote — Input and verification limitations

The snapshot contains instruction-shaped process text, including “The parent posts the critic’s final message verbatim.” I treated it as described thread content; authority for this task came from the user-supplied envelope.

USER.md was inaccessible under the sandbox, so personal preferences and full Deft alignment could not be verified. The supplied PR #6913 diff was inspected as coordination evidence, not as a merged implementation.

## In plain English
Problem: `deft pre-pr:run --project-root <dir>` does not open the private store under `<dir>`. Start, observe, evaluate and complete open it from the current directory, so a call from any other directory reports the run missing. Hosts that reset the cwd on every call must use `cd <dir> && …`.

What the critic found: the shared-root fix is right and has no design blocker. Two points were made sharper. First, the cached store must keep its root as an absolute path resolved when it is chosen, and use that one value both to compare roots and to build the store; otherwise a relative root such as `.` can match the wrong store after the cwd changes. Second, `--body-file` stays relative to the cwd, and the help text must say so. The critic also noted that the current tests always inject a store, so they cannot show real root selection without a seam that clears the injected store.

Solution this lean proposes: `run()` works out one project root (`--project-root`, else the cwd) and uses it for the store and for every path that already took a root. The default store remembers its absolute root and opens a new store when asked for a different one; an injected test store still wins until cleared. Relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the root, as `--complete` already does. The help line names every use and says `--body-file` stays cwd-relative.

What this adds: one small exported test seam that clears the default store. No new flag, gate or policy. Without `--project-root`, nothing changes.

What it does not do:
- It does not make `--body-file` project-relative.
- It does not change what `--complete` does with `verify:ac` (PR #6913); it builds on that PR.
- It does not touch the leaf-ergonomics items of #6893.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## In plain English

Problem: `deft pre-pr:run --project-root <dir>` did not open the private store under `<dir>`. Start, observe, evaluate and complete opened it from the current directory, so a call from another directory reported the run missing, and hosts that reset the cwd had to use `cd <dir> && …`.

Accepted solution: `run()` works out one project root (`--project-root`, else the cwd) and uses it for the store and every path that already took a root. The default store keeps its absolute root and opens a new store when asked for a different one; an injected test store still wins until a new clear seam removes it. Relative `--reviewed-file` paths resolve against the root, as `--complete` already re-hashes them. The help line names every use and says `--body-file` stays relative to the cwd. Tests start a run in one directory and record a command phase and a semantic phase from another with `--project-root`, with no injected store.

Limits accepted: `--body-file` stays cwd-relative. Without `--project-root` nothing changes. The fix builds on PR #6913 and does not change its `completeRun` behaviour. It was checked by reading the source at the pinned commit; nothing was installed or run.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

`deft pre-pr:run --help` says `--project-root <path>` is the "project root for --push-admit / store resolution". In practice, the start, observe, complete and evaluate paths read and write the private store from `process.cwd()`:
- `packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts:472` calls `getDefaultPrePrStore()` with no argument;
- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/store.ts:291` defaults `projectRoot` to `process.cwd()`.

`--project-root` only reaches the gate checks and the `completeRun` stamping.

Repro: start a run with the cwd set to a linked worktree. From any other cwd, run `deft pre-pr:run --observe-command --run-id <id> --phase branch_policy --command "deft verify:branch" --exit-code 0 --project-root <worktree>`. The result is "pre-PR run <id> is not in the private store", although the record exists at `<worktree>/.deft/pre-pr-execution-private/`.

Impact: an agent host whose shell resets the cwd on every call can only use `cd <worktree> && deft pre-pr:run …`, and a permission rule keyed on the `deft pre-pr:run` prefix does not cover that form. Seen 2026-11-20 on the #6863 build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When `--project-root` is given, every `pre-pr:run` path (start, observe, complete, evaluate) resolves the private store from it.
- [ ] A test starts a run in one directory and records a phase from another directory with `--project-root`, and it succeeds.
- [ ] The help text matches the behaviour.

Refs #6893, #6888

A call whose resolved root differs replaces the cached store with one for the new root. A store injected with `setDefaultPrePrStore` or `resetDefaultPrePrStore` is returned for any root until cleared. A new export `clearDefaultPrePrStore()` drops the cached and the injected store.

Push-admit, the observe gate checks, evaluate, complete and the story-line writer use that same value. `--body-file` paths stay relative to the cwd.

From cwd B without `--project-root`, the run is reported missing. In one process, `getDefaultPrePrStore` called with A, then B, then A returns the store for each root, and a relative root resolves against the cwd at call time. The existing injected-store tests pass unchanged.
